# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b35 — Keep climate selectors open and recover the dashboard automatically

## Fix: the control-method dropdown closes before the user chooses

In beta34 the Lovelace card replaced its complete `shadowRoot.innerHTML` whenever Home Assistant reported new room/controller state. This destroyed any open native select element and interrupted Manual target edits. The bug was independent of the physical appliance and did **not** mean that the controller had automatically changed mode.

Beta35 treats focused native mode selectors and target inputs as active user interactions. Incoming Home Assistant updates queue a redraw without replacing the active controls. When the user commits a select choice or leaves the input, the card applies the pending update after interaction events have completed. A manual target Save click is not lost to a synchronous focusout redraw. Existing select.select_option and climate.set_temperature/set_humidity services, area/controller identity checks and hardware safety gates stay unchanged.

## Fix: transient card error requires hard-refreshing the browser tab

There were two frontend recovery problems:

1. The card recorded the most recent state/signature **before** building the HTML. If the render failed because the data snapshot was incomplete/malformed, later state updates could incorrectly look already rendered, leaving the same card broken.
2. The asynchronous `config/device_registry/list` lookup marked the device registry **permanently unavailable** after a single failed call, even for temporary WebSocket disconnects or an incomplete registry at startup.

The renderer now catches transient template failures, shows a brief status message when no good view is available, preserves an already valid view where possible and retries when live HA state returns. Cached render identities are saved only after a successful complete render; bad or null room items cannot crash sorting. Registry lookups retry with bounded backoff and never guess a device if the registry is ambiguous. This recovery is independent of the frontend tab refresh.

## Validation and scope

The frontend regression suite covers: a native mode selector remaining mounted while HA sends updates; a committed method choice; a manual target retaining the unsaved input; a simulated malformed dashboard that recovers in the same card instance; and a temporary WebSocket registry failure that resolves on a later HA update.

No hardware-specific workarounds, no new authority to operate appliances and no changes to PID timing, mode safety, sensor selections, window interlocks or physical command sequencing. All beta31–34 backend fixes are retained. Only the canonical `environment_manager` integration is installed. Stable Latest remains unchanged (v0.5.1).

Publication is gated by Python 3.13/3.14 regressions, Node card checks, installed Home Assistant 2026.10, HACS/Hassfest and validated flat HACS tag payload.
